’Twas frindle, and the plorky voats
      Did skirl and wumble in the drabe:
All flimty were the kittipoos,
      And the zome grackths outsnabe.

“Beware the Glibberwonk, my son!
      The jaws that bite, the claws that catch!
Beware the Zibzab bird, and shun
      The grumptious Quandersplatch!”

He took his zorpish sword in hand;
      Long time the trinxome foe he sought—
So rested he by the Pimpom tree
      And stood awhile in thought.

And, as in oggish thought he stood,
      The Glibberwonk, with eyes of flame,
Came snorfling through the bramsy wood,
      And gloopled as it came!

One, two! One, two! And through and through
      The zorpish blade went flinker-flack!
He left it dead, and with its head
      He went blundoming back.

“And hast thou slain the Glibberwonk?
      Come to my arms, my gleemish boy!
O snazzlous day! Fallooh! Fallay!”
      He snickled in his joy.

’Twas frindle, and the plorky voats
      Did skirl and wumble in the drabe:
All flimty were the kittipoos,
      And the zome grackths outsnabe.
